transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I'm here because... well, I just can't shake this feeling that work isn't safe anymore. And honestly, I feel like I'm somehow damaged now. It's like the competent person who just got promoted isn't really there anymore. I don't know, it's just been really hard to deal with.
Did something traumatic happen at work that made you start feeling this way?
Yes, it did. There was a break-in while I was at the office for an overnight deployment. This has all been going on since then, which was about two years and four months ago.
Do you have unwanted memories of the break-in that suddenly come back into your mind?

Yes, I do. It usually happens when something specific sets it off... like hearing a badge scanner beep, or heavy footsteps out in the hallway. Even just getting a late-night deployment alert on my phone can do it. 

When that happens, it's like I'm suddenly put right back in that office. My chest gets really tight, and the image of the guard on the floor just... it just cuts through whatever I’m trying to do at the time.
Since the break-in, have you been avoiding places, situations, or reminders that bring it back to mind?

Yes, definitely. I try to avoid anything that reminds me of it. I've been trading my overnight shifts and pushing back on the late release windows whenever possible. And when I do have to go in, I take the side entrance or just work from home if I can. Walking through that main lobby after dark... I just can't do it. It makes me feel like I'm going to completely come apart.
Since the break-in, have you been feeling jumpy or easily startled?

Yes, I have. I'm just always on edge now. Whether I'm on the train, in meetings, or even just at lunch with my team... I automatically clock the exits. I watch to see who is standing too close to me, and I keep one ear tuned to any noises out in the hallway instead of just being fully present. I'm constantly scanning my surroundings.
Since the break-in, have you been blaming yourself or feeling like you’re permanently damaged because of what happened?

Yes, I do blame myself. I just keep thinking that if I had insisted on better security for the overnight deployment, or... or if I had called for help sooner, the guard might not have been hurt so badly. Even though part of me knows I was just hiding and completely terrified at the time, I still feel like I should have done something differently.
Since the break-in, have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy?

No, not really. I mean, I still like doing the things I usually do. I still play video games and read when I'm safe at home. It's really just... being out or at the office that's the problem. But my actual interests haven't really changed.
Since the break-in, have you had nightmares about what happened?

Yes, I have. Most nights I just lie there replaying little details from work, or... or I'll jolt awake from these dreams where I’m hiding under the conference table again. It's really frustrating because even when I do manage to get six or seven hours of sleep, I wake up feeling like I never really powered down.
Since the break-in, have you been feeling a lot of fear, horror, anger, guilt, or shame?

I mean, besides the guilt I already mentioned about the guard... and being scared when I think about going back to the office... not really. I don't feel angry about it, and I don't think I feel ashamed. It's really just... just that specific guilt, and the fear of being back in that building. But I don't walk around feeling horrified or angry all day, if that's what you mean.
Since the break-in, have you been feeling down or depressed most days?

No, I wouldn't say I feel depressed most days. I mean, I'm definitely stressed out and tired from not sleeping well, but I don't really feel down in that way. My mood is generally okay when I'm just at home doing my own thing. It's really just the anxiety about work and what happened, not a general sadness.
